final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 is the catalytic lysine that forms the internal aldimine with PLP; its mutation to alanine abolishes the Schiff base linkage essential for all CBS catalytic steps. AlphaMissense 0.987, MSA entropy 0.056, and ESM-1v 0.000 all converge on extreme functional disruption.

C52 is a heme axial ligand in the regulatory domain; its mutation disrupts heme binding, destabilizing the N-terminal domain and impairing the conformational activation required for catalysis. AlphaMissense 0.951 and ESM-1v 0.0004 confirm strong disruption.

R266 resides in the catalytic core and participates in substrate binding/stabilization of the PLP-substrate complex. AlphaMissense 0.929, MSA conservation 0.083, and ESM-1v 0.0002 all support severe functional impairment.

stop_reason.detail: All three evidence dimensions converge on the same top-3 ranking with no remaining ambiguity; further tool calls would not alter the outcome.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the catalytic lysine that forms the internal aldimine with PLP; mutation to alanine abolishes Schiff base formation and thus all CBS enzymatic activity.
K119 is the catalytic lysine that forms the internal aldimine with PLP; mutation to alanine abolishes the Schiff base linkage essential for CBS activity.
Highest AlphaMissense LOF score (0.987) combined with very low evolutionary tolerance (freq 0.056) at the PLP-binding lysine makes this the strongest LOF candidate.

ESM-1v score of 0.000 confirms extreme implausibility, fully consistent with LOF at the catalytic lysine. All three orthogonal evidence dimensions (AlphaMissense 0.987, MSA 0.056, PLM 0.000) converge strongly.
Gly116 is in the PLP-binding motif (Gly-rich loop); substitution with alanine may distort the cofactor-binding pocket and impair PLP coordination.
G116 is in the PLP-binding pocket; glycine-to-alanine may disrupt local backbone conformation needed for cofactor binding.
Moderate phenotype score (0.771) and low evolutionary tolerance support LOF but weaker than top candidates.
ESM-1v score of 0.0001 confirms disruption, but AlphaMissense 0.771 is the weakest among active candidates, keeping it at rank 5.
Cys52 is a conserved cysteine in the N-terminal heme-binding region; mutation may disrupt heme coordination and allosteric regulation, contributing to loss of function.
C52 coordinates the heme iron in the N-terminal regulatory domain; loss may destabilize the heme and indirectly affect catalytic domain conformation.
Very high phenotype score (0.951) supports LOF, but MSA shows 22% homolog frequency for Ala at this position, suggesting some evolutionary tolerance; net still strongly supports LOF.
ESM-1v score of 0.0004 confirms extreme disruption at heme-ligand C52. Combined with AlphaMissense 0.951, this remains a strong LOF candidate.
Arg266 is involved in substrate (homocysteine) recognition; alanine substitution removes a key electrostatic interaction for substrate binding.
R266 is near the active site and may participate in substrate binding or transition-state stabilization.
High phenotype score (0.929) and low evolutionary tolerance (freq 0.083) in the catalytic core domain strongly support LOF.
ESM-1v score of 0.0002 confirms extreme implausibility. AlphaMissense 0.929 and MSA 0.083 both support strong functional disruption at this catalytic domain residue.
Glu131 participates in PLP binding and active-site architecture; alanine substitution may weaken cofactor affinity and destabilize the active conformation.
E131 may participate in the hydrogen-bond network around the PLP-binding site.
